A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAS framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original RAS results on seven benchmarks, component ablations, sensitivity studies, training curves, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains the original RAS experiments and reports additional baseline results and triple-extractor throughput.

M1.justification: The planning, retrieval, triple extraction, graph accumulation, answering, and multitask-training procedures are retained. Question-specific replaces query-specific terminology. The maximum-iteration stopping condition added to Section 3.3 was already documented in v2's inference settings; the closed-source implementation receives clarification rather than an established procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HotpotQA-SUBQ, ARC-Easy, ASQA, and WikiOFGraph training coverage and the same seven evaluation benchmarks. Wikipedia knowledge sources and represented task categories remain unchanged. The new cost estimates concern the existing Wikipedia setting.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ReAct and IRCoT with both Sonnet-3.5 and 7B models. It removes Alpaca-7B/13B with and without retrieval, RECOMP-7B, retrieval-augmented ChatGPT, and Search-R1-7B. This substantially revises the comparator set. SuRe-GPT becomes SuRe-GPT-4o with identical scores, indicating clarification rather than replacement.

E3.justification: v3 adds throughput evaluation and a Wikipedia-scale resource-estimation protocol with corpus-size, pricing, and processing assumptions. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, training budgets, retrieval settings, and prompts are retained. Section 4.1 additionally lists Sonnet-4.5 as an inference configuration, although corresponding results are absent.

E4.justification: New Appendix G adds estimated indexing-cost comparisons and sensitivity discussion concerning model choice, chunk size, and prompt optimization. Table 3 extends the existing extractor-selection analysis to efficiency. Component ablations, role swapping, graph abundance, data scaling, context-depth analysis, and error cases are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix G newly reports cost uncertainty ranges reflecting model choice, optimization, and implementation variation. These are assumption-dependent ranges, not statistical confidence intervals. The existing five-shuffle averaging practice is unchanged, with no added seed counts or repeated-run statistical testing.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds and removes substantial baseline result blocks and fills Self-RAG-13B's missing 2WQA F1 and ELI5 ROUGE/MAUVE entries with 26.9, 18.7, and 38.5. Table 3 adds throughput of 166.0, 4,885.3, and 68.2 tokens/s for Flan-T5, LLaMA-3.2-3B, and Sonnet-3.5. Appendix G adds cost, compute-time, and storage estimates. Retained RAS benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, framework equations, sample-labeling algorithm, and evaluation-metric formulas retain their mathematical substance. Neither version develops theorems or proofs. The new cost calculations are resource estimates rather than new formal properties or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: Abstract/introduction gains change from 6.4% open-source and 7.0% proprietary to 7.0% and 8.7%, although v3's conclusion reports 6.4% and 7.0%. Efficiency and scalability become explicit contribution claims. The first general-generation application claim for Graph LLMs and the conclusion's high-stakes suitability assertion disappear, while the central dynamic-graph contribution remains.

C2.justification: The introduction adds an explanation that question-specific graphs resolve ambiguous or contradictory relations in global graphs. Extractor-selection discussion now emphasizes the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff. Appendix G adds interpretations about deployment affordability and cost sensitivity. Existing limitations and interpretations of the retained ablations and error cases remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 removes the two direct links to trained triple-extractor checkpoints from the training appendix, while retaining the overall code/data repository link. It explicitly states that Sonnet-3.5 RAS omits graph encoding/projection and identifies SuRe-GPT as GPT-4o. Cost-estimation assumptions are added; most hardware, software, hyperparameter, and processing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds S3 and AI-SearchPlanner discussion, plus IRCoT, LoRA, and Sonnet-4.5 references; PaLM, Search-R1, and RECOMP references disappear. It elaborates cost-based positioning against GraphRAG and HippoRAG and withdraws the first-application novelty claim. The broader positioning around dynamic versus static graph construction is retained.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting and condensation. Terminology shifts from query-specific graphs and modules toward question-specific graphs and steps, and Section 4 is reorganized into settings and results. Author/affiliation information changes, and acknowledgments, ethics, and LLM-use statements are added.

P2.justification: The combined overview becomes a redrawn workflow figure and a separate multitask-learning figure. The future-extensions illustration is removed. Table 1 is reorganized into closed-source and open-source blocks, Table 3 gains an efficiency column, and Appendix G adds a cost table and chart. Conference formatting also changes typography, headers, and content placement throughout.

improvement.justification: Clearer framework diagrams, relevant iterative baselines, and extractor throughput improve exposition and evidence. However, v3 removes earlier comparisons and checkpoint links while introducing inconsistent headline gains and mentioning Sonnet-4.5 evaluation without corresponding results. The new cost analysis supplies assumptions but remains an estimate rather than a measured system comparison. These benefits and reporting weaknesses coexist without a reliably assessable net direction in overall quality.
